full_judgment:
AKM Zahiru1 Hoque J : This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Memo No. Bichar-7/2N- 27/2012-256 dated 11.-4-2013 (Annexure-C) issued by the Respondent No.2 bifurcating No.4 Eyarpur Union into two Nikah Registry areas and thereby asking the Sub-Registry to prepare panel of the applicants should riot be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts, relevant for the purpose of disposal of the Rule, in short, is that in pursuance of Memo dated 26-7-2012) the Ministry of Law, justice and Parliamentary Affairs has appointed the petitioner as Nikah Registrar of No. 4 Eyarpur Union under Police Station-Ashulia.

3. Since the date of appointment the petitioner has been performing his function with full satisfaction of the authority and of the local inhabitants.

4. While the petitioner had been performing his function with full satisfaction of the authority the local MP issued a Demi Official (DO) letter recommending to bifurcate No.4 Eyarpur Union but the then Assistant Secretary of Bichar Shaka- 7 of respondent No.1 kept the said letter in record commenting that there is no scope of bifurcating an Union as per the provisions of Muslim Bibaho o Talaq (Nibandhan) Bidhimala, 2009 and on 12- 9-2012 the said information has been duly Communicated to the local MP vide Memo No. Bichar-7/2N-27/2012-645.

5. On 11-4-2013 respondent No. 2 issued Memo No. Bichar-7/2N-27/2012-256 (hereinafter referred as impugned memo) bifurcating No. 4 Eyarpur Union into two Nikah Registry areas of which the new one consisting of Wards Nos. 6, 7, 8 and 9 and asking the Sub-Registrar to prepare panel of applicants for the newly created area.

6. That the copy of the impugned order has been issued only to the Sub-Registrar and the petitioner has not been served with any copy of the impugned memo. Therefore, he has collected an attested copy of the same from the office of Respondent No. 2.

7. Being influenced by an interested quarter including the local Member of Parliament (MP), Respondent No.2 has issued the impugned memo and therefore, the impugned memo is malafide and illegal.

8. The petitioner's office is situated in Ward No.6 whereas Ward No.6 has been taken away from his jurisdiction without application of mind and therefore the impugned order is malafide.

9. That under Rule 13(Uma) of the Muslim Bibaho OTalaq (Nibandhan) Bidhimala, 2009 a Nikah Registrar of an Union is entitle to hold the entire Union and therefore bifurcation of No.4, Eyarpur Union into two Nikah Registry areas is without lawful authority.

10. The Sub-Registrar has not yet published any appointment notice nor even has prepared any panel. The petitioner is still performing his function in the entire Union and therefore, the impugned Memo is required to be stayed.

11. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned Memo dated 11-4-2013 issued by the Respondent No. 2 the petitioner moved this application before this Court under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained the present Rule and stay of the operation of the impugned order.

12. On the other hand, an affidavit in opposition has been filed on behalf of the Respondent No.1 through learned Deputy Attorney-General denying all the material allegations of the writ petition and stating inter-alia that the No. 4 Eyarpur Union is an over populated developing industrial and residential area and about fifteen lac people are residing there and the population of that area are being increased rapidly now it became impossible for one Nikah Registrars to give service properly to so many people in respect of registration of their marriages and divorces and considering the problems, harassment and inconvenience of the people of No.4 Eyarpur Union and as per demand of the people the Member of Parliament of that constituency made application to the Hon'ble Minister as well as to the Secretary, Ministry of law, Justice and parliamentary Affair on 29-7-2012 to bifurcate No.4 Eyarpur Union into two Nikah Registry areas and appoint two Nikah Registrars for the interest of the public. Considering the necessity, the impugned memo has been issued by the Respondents upon bifurcating the said union and thereby creating a new area consisting of Ward Nos. 6, 7, 8 and 9 and asking to prepare and send a panel for appointment of a Nikah Registrar for the newly created area for the interest of the people.

13. It is stated that the impugned memo has been issued for the interest of the local people to save them from harassment and for the convenience of the inhabitants to have smooth service of the Nikah Registrar and the same has been issued legally as per provision of second proviso of section 4 of the Muslim Marriage and Divorces (Registration) Act, 1974.

14. It is staled that the Ward Nos. 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 have been kept for the petitioner considering that the petitioner is the resident of village- Burirpara under Ward. No. 5 of No. 4 Eyarpur Union.

15. Mr Mohammad Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, after drawing our attention to the different Annexure as annexed with his writ petition, submits that the petitioner vide his appointment letter issued under the provision of Muslim Marriage and Divorce Registration Act, 1974 read with rule 13(Uma) of the Muslim Marriage and Divorce Registration Rules, 2009 has been appointed Nikah Registrar for the entire No.4 Eyarpur union and there is no provision of curtailment of his jurisdiction under Rule 13(Uma). Hence the government has acted illegally in curtailing the area of his Nikah Registrary. Such curtailment of area by the said impugned order is totally contrary to the provision of Rule 13 (Uma) of the Muslim Marriage and Divorce Registration Rules, 2009 and thereby asking to prepare a panel for the said newly Created area before the said post became vacant after the retirement of the petitioner or otherwise he is found to be unfit for carrying out the business of registering the Marriage and Divorce of the peoples of the locality. He further submits that the Rules 13(Uma) has specifically mentioned that one whole Union shall be the jurisdiction of one Nikha Registrar which is other than City Corporation or Municipal area and that is the maximum or minimum limit of the licence as issued by the Government in favour of the petitioner. Thus curtailment of area of the petitioner by the impugned memo has not been done in accordance with any provision of law and Rules relating to appointment of the Nikha Registrar of the Muslim Marriage and Divorce Registration Act and as such the said impugned memo is liable to be declared without lawful authority and is of no legal effect., He further submits that Rules 13(Uma) is the absolute and conclusive provision of law under which by the authority look decision about the area for the purpose of issuance of license/Certificate in favour of the petitioner and subsequent curtailment of the area upon bifurcating the said union into two Nikah Registries areas nothing but gross violation of the Rules 13(Uma) of the Muslim Marriage and Divorce Registration Rules, 2009. He then submits that since the petitioner is performing as the Nikha Registrar and there is no allegation of misconduct and he is per- forming as Nikha Registrar of the said Union within full satisfaction of the local inhabitants, issuance of the impugned order is without lawful authority and is of no legal effect, In support of such submissions the learned Advocate for the petitioner referred the case of Kazi Imamuddin Bhuiya vs Government of Bangladesh, reported in 10 BLC (AD) 2005; MdSaiful Islam vs Government of the people s Republic of Bangladesh, reported in 18 MLR (HCD) 2013, 481; Syed Md Anwarul Haque vs Bangladesh, reported in 57 DLR 248; Hafez Md Bazlur Rahman vs Bangladesh Represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Law, justice and in parliamentary affairs, reported in 56 DLR 444; Fazlur Rahman and 38 others vs Government of Bangladesh, reported in 53 DLR 237; Kazi Akbar Hossain vs Shamsuddin Ahmed reported in 31 DLR 430; and the Case of Achia Khatun vs Soleman Ali, reported in 2 BLC (1997).

16. Along with the above decisions he also referred to an Unreported judgment dated 12-12-2012 passed by the another Bench of his Division in Writ Petitioner No. 9833 of 2011.

17. Per contra Mr Md Al-Amin Sarker, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 1 submits that the second proviso to section 4 of the Muslim Marriage and Divorce (Registration) Act, 1974 has given unfettered and unrestricted power to the Government to curtail, extend or otherwise alter the limit or area for which a Nikah Registrar has been licensed whenever the Government deems fit to do so which has been approved by the Appellate Division in the cases of Moulvi Md Khurshid Alam vs Bangladesh, reported in 50 DLR (AD) 82; Rais Uddin vs Bangladesh reported in 51 DLR (AD) 152; Kazi Md Amirul Islam vs Bangladesh, reported in 16 BLD (AD) 110; Md Nasir Uddin vs Government of Bangladesh, reported in 16 BLT (AD) (2008) 151 and in the case of Md Emran Hossain vs Bangladesh Government, reported in V ADC (2008) 880. He further submits that the language of section 4 of the Act, 1974 clearly expressed the legislative intent for determination of any area for the purpose of granting license and appointing Nikah Registrar and also for extension, curtailment or otherwise alteration of the limits of any particular area, by unambiguous terms and the rules which have been framed under the said Parent Act, by the rule making authority are always subordinate to the express provision of the Act, and the provisions of the Act cannot be superseded by the rules. In other words, the provisions of the Act cannot be circumscribed by the rules framed under the enactment. In that view of the matter, the provisions of section 4 will prevail upon the rules. Although in rule 13(Uma) the area for which the Nikah Registrar may be licensed has been specified, but in view of the power as conferred by the legislature, is second proviso of section 4 of the Act, the Government may extend cur- tailor otherwise alter the limits of any area for which a Nikah Registrar has been licensed, and consequently the Government having such unfettered and unrestricted power, has bifurcated the Union of the petitioner and thereby curtailed and altered limits of the area of the petitioner in accordance with law.

18. Therefore, he submits that the area determined by the relevant rules regulating the area of territorial jurisdiction are not mandatory rather the same is directory. So far the exercise of the power by the Government under section 4 of the Act is concerned he submits that it is unrestricted and same cannot be curtailed by the rules. He further submits that the No.4 Eyarpur Union is an over populated developing industrial and residential area and about fifteen lac people are residing there and the population of that area are being increased rapidly and now it has become impossible for one Nikah Registrar to give service properly to so many people in respect of registration of their marriages and divorces and considering the problems, harassment and considering the necessity, the impugned memo has been issued by the Respondents thereby bifurcating the Union into two Nlkah Registry areas with Ward Nos. 6, 7, 8 and 9 creating a new area and asking to prepare and send a panel for appointment of a Nikah Registrar for the newly created area for the interest of the people.

19. He further submits that stated the impugned memo has been issued for the interest of the local people to save them from harassment and for the convenience of the inhabitants to have smooth service of the Nikah Registrar and the same has been issued legally as per provision of second proviso of section 4 of the Muslim marriage and Divorces (Registration) Act, 1974. He further submits that the Ward Nos. 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 have been kept for the petitioner considering that the petitioner is the resident of village-Burirpara- Burirpara under Ward No. 5 of No. 4 Eyarpur Union. He further submits that the 2nd proviso to section 4 of the Muslim Marriage and Divorce (Registration) Act, 1974 has. given power to the Government to extend, curtail or otherwise limit any area for which a Nikah Registrar has been licensed whenever the Government deems fit to do so. Hence the grounds taken in the Writ Petition are misconceived and not entertain able in law. He Further' submitted that the Government issues licence to a Nikah Registrar who acts as Government's agent and gets commission for registering marriage in the area for which he a has been issued a licence and therefore the Nikah Registrars are mere licences and agents of the Government and thus no question of violation of fundamental right and/or natural justice arises in passing an order, of the curtailment of the area under his jurisdiction and as such the rule is liable to be discharged.

20. Heard the learned Advocate of both the sides, perused the affidavit-in-opposition, supplementary affidavit-in opposition filed by the learned Deputy Attorney-General, affidavit-in-reply filed by the learned Advocate for the petitioner and other materials on record.

21. Admittedly the petitioner was appointed a Nikha Registrar of the entire No.4 Eyarpur Union in pursuance of Memo dared 26-7-2012 by the respondent No.1 and since then he is functioning as a Nikha Registrar of the said No. 4 Eyarpur Union under Police Station-Ashulia, Savar, Dhaka. The petitioner challenged the sub- sequent order of curtailment of some area of the said Union from the area of the petitioner upon bifurcating No. 4 Eyarpur Union 'into two Nikha Registrar areas with a direction upon the Sub  Registrar to prepare a panel of the applicants to appoint a Nikha Registrar for the newly treated area. The said letter has been issued under the signature of the respondent 2 vide Memo dated 11-4-2013, Annexure-C to the writ petition which is under challenge On the ground that since the petitioner has been appointed as Nikha Registrar under section 4 of the Nikha Registrar Act, 1974 read with Rules 13(Uma) of the Muslim Marriage and Divorce Registration Rules; 2009 there, is no scope of curtailment of the area from the petitioner As such the' impugned order is without jurisdiction and is of no legal effect. Now the vital issue before this Court is whether the Government is empowered to pass such order in bifurcating the said Union into two Nikha Registrar areas or not. It appears from the affidavit in opposition on behalf of the respondent No.1 that No.4 Eyarpur Union is a over populated, developing, industrial and residential area with about 15 lac people residing there and the population of that area are being increased rapidly. Thus now it has become impossible on the part of one Nikah Registrar to give service properly to the people in respect of registration of marriage and divorce. Accordingly for the interest of the people and as per demand of local people the Member of the Parliament made an application to the Hon'ble Minister, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary affairs as well as to the respondent No. 1 on 29-7-2012 with a request to bifurcate No.4 Eyarpur Union Nikha Registrar area and thereby appoint two Nikha Registrars for the interest of the local public. After considering the necessity the impugned memo has been issued by the respondent upon creating a new area with word Nos. 6, 7, 8 and 9 of the said Union and asking to prepare and send a panel for appointment of a Nikha Registrar for the new area for the interest of the local people. These material facts in respect of increasing of the population of the said union has nor been denied by the petitioner in any point of time neither by the affidavit- in reply nor by filing any material-on-record. Therefore it is admitted that No.4 Eyarpur Union is a over populated, industrial area with about 15 lac people residing there.

22. For the purpose of registration of marriage and divorce the legislature enacted the acts namely The Muslim Marriage and Divorce Act, 1974 (hereinafter mentioned as Act, 1974) wherein section 4 deals with appointment of Nikah Registrar. Subsequently, for the legal necessity The Muslim Marriage and Divorce Registration (Amendment) Ordinance 1982 has been enacted which came to force on 1-12-1982. In order to carry out the purpose and its object effectively the second proviso to section 4 of the said Act, 1974 has been incorporated by amendment in the said Ordinance of 1982. In order to carry out the purpose of the said Act of Parliament, the Government has framed Rules namely Muslim marriage and Divorce Registration Rules, 2009 which came to force on 10-8-2009. In the said Rules of 2009 Rule 13 provides the jurisdiction of the Nikha Registrar for effective, easy and smooth registration of the marriage and divorce in any particular area. For proper and effective consideration of the matter the provision of section 4 of said Act, and rule 13(Uma) of the said rules are quoted below;

"4. Nikah Registrars-For the purpose of Registration of marriages under this Act, the Government shall grant licences to such number of persons, to be called Nikah Registrars, as it may deem necessary for such areas as it may specify; Provided that not more than one Nikah Registrar shall be licensed for anyone area. Provided further that the Government may, whenever it deems fit so to do, extend, curtail or otherwise alter the limits of any area for which Nikah Registrar has been Licensed."

The relevant Rule 13 of rules 2009 is as under;

১৩। অধিক্ষেত্র।- এই বিধিমালার অধীন প্রদত্ত নিকাহ রেজিস্ট্রারের লাইসেন্স যাহা কিছ্ইু থাকুক না কেন, একজন নিকাহ রেজিস্ট্রারকে নিম্নবর্ণিত এলাকার জন্য লাইসেন্স প্রদান করা যাইবে, যথা:-

ক) সিটিকর্পোরেশনের ক্ষেত্রে, একটি ওয়ার্ড,

খ) ক’ শ্রেণীর পৌরসভা ক্ষেত্রে, দুইটি ওয়ার্ড,

গ) খ’ শ্রেণীর পৌরসভার ক্ষেত্রে, তিনটি ওয়ার্ড

ঘ) গ’ শ্রেণীর পৌরসভার ক্ষেত্রে সমগ্র এলাকা,

ঙ)       ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ এলাকার ক্ষেত্রে একটি ইউনিয়ন।

23. It appears from the above mentioned pro- vision Of the Act, that only the Government is empowered to grant license to such number of persons as Nikha Registrar as if may deem necessary for such area as it may specify. And second proviso of section 4 of the said Act,1974 by which the Government is also specially empowered to extend, curtail or otherwise alter the limits of any area for which a Nikha Registrar has been licensed, On the other hand rule 13(Uma) of the Muslim Marriage and Divorce Registration Rules, 2009 provides that in respect of one Union one of Nikha Registrar may be licensed; So, the second proviso to section 4 of the Act empowered the government to extend, curtail, or otherwise alter the limit of a Nikha Registrar already licensed under Rule 13(Uma) of Muslim Marriage and Divorce Registration Rules 2009.

24. It appears that the petitioner admittedly Was appointed as Nikha Registrar for and on behalf of the Government for the entire No. 4 Eyarpur Union. He performed his duties as the Nikah registrar for registering marriages/ divorcees for and on behalf of the Government in the specified area of his jurisdiction, for a Union. As he was issued licences as such, his position is not better than those of a licensce conferred with the right to do something which otherwise he would not have legal power to do. Conferring of such right is a special privilege rather than a right common to all. It is often required as a condition precedent to the right to carry on his business within the jurisdiction and as such the petitioner does not acquire any vested right to invoke Article 102 of the constitution nor he is entitled to a prior notice to show cause before the curtailment of the area of his jurisdiction.

As he was issued licences as such, his position is not better than those of a licensce conferred with the right to do something which otherwise he would not have legal power to do. Conferring of such right is a special privilege rather than aright common to all. It is often required as a condition precedent to the right to carry on his business within the jurisdiction and as such the petitioner does not acquire any vested right to invoke Article 102 of the constitution nor he is entitled to a prior notice to show cause before the curtailment of the area of his jurisdiction

25. It further appears that he license of the petitioner so granted empowers the Nikah Registrar to act on 'behalf" of the Government to registrar marriage or divorce in lieu of fees to the Government and the, Nikah Registrar receiving the commission only. Thus a Nikah Registrar, in, fact is an agent of the Government and the Nikah Registrar's licence is also liable to be revoked, suspended; annulled by following the procedure provided under rule 11 of Rules, 2009. In such view of the.matter we find that; the Government has authority to curtail extend or otherwise alter the limit of any Nikah Registrar any time without any prior notice.

<u>26. From the first part of the section 4 of the Act, 1974 read with Rule 13(Uma) it appears that the government is empowered, to grant license of a Nikha Registrar for not more than one Union that is government is preventedtoGive licensefor more than one Union in favour of one licensee i.e. the maximum limit of Nikah registrar. But Rule 13(Uma) did not mention any minimumlimit Lei the governments is not barred, to issue licnese to more than one Nikah registrar in one Union if it deem fit necessary. Which will be clear from the second proviso of section 4 of the Act, 1974 (which is the parent law). The same has given the authority to the government to curtail, alter or otherwise if it think .necessary to issue such license-by curtailment of the area from the area of any existing Nikha Registrar for any legal cause. The said power of the government, as provided in 2nd proviso of section 4 of the said Act-cannot be knocked down by rule 13(Uma) or any, other, rules of Rules, 2009 (which is a subordinate Legislation).The rules 2009 is the product of the parent Act only to carry out the object of the parent Act, As such the Nikha Registrar is empowered, to act on behalf of the government to registrar marriage and divorce having 'acquired a right in pursuance of license only not beyond that. So the entire provisions of section 4 of Act, 1974 clearly shows that the government always "has' got the authority to extend, curtailor limit the jurisdiction of any Nikah Registrar' if it thinks necessary. The said statutory power of the government will always override any rules including rule 13 (Uma) of the Muslim Marriage and Divorce Registration Rules, 2009 made under the authority of section 14 of the Act of 1974 which has given power to the government to make rules for the purpose of effective application of the Act, As such determination of jurisdiction or area for which Nikah registrar is appointed has been specified in the force of sub- section 2 of suction 14 of the said Act, read with rule 13(Uma) of Rules, 2009. In rule (Uma) relates to the maximum area for which a Nikah Registrar is appointed.</u>

27. Thus 2nd proviso of section 4 having empowered the Government to extend, alter curtail or limit any area of a Nikah Registrar and considering the trend of increase of the inhabitants of No. 4 Eyarpur Union, at present which is about fifteen lacs and considering the demand of the people curtailment of the'. Petitioners Nikah registries area, upon bifurcating the said union for legal necessity is very such within the legal authority. The said power of the Government in respect of curtailment of existing area of the petitioner has been given by the Parliament for the purpose of carrying out the registration of marriage and Divorce amongst the peoples of that area smoothly and effectively. The said power of the Government cannot be curtailed by the subordinate legislation- i.e. Rule 13(Uma) of Rules, 2009 as framed by the Government. Rather when any rule of Rules, 2009 is found to be inconsistent with any provision of the Act, 1974 in that case the provisions or the parent act shall prevail upon the provisions of any rule including rule 13(Uma) of Rules, 2009.

28. In such view of the matter; we hold that there has been no violation of the principle of natral justice nor there is any question of violation of vested right of the petitioner nor even the provision of Rule 13(Uma) of the Rules, 2009 has been violated in issuing the impugned memo dated 11-4-2013 (Annexure-C) by the Government in the way of passing the order of curtailment of the area of jurisdiction of the petitioner for the above legal reasons.

29. We have gone through the decisions as cited above by the learned Advocate for the petitioner and by the Learned Deputy Attorney General on behalf of the respondents and after perusal of all the said decisions we find support in the case of Kazi Md Aminul Islam vs Bangladesh as reported in 16 BID (AD) 110 Wherein it has been held that 'it also authorizes the Government to curtail the jurisdiction of any Union Parishad and declare any part of if as an "Urban area" and thereafter include the said area in Pourasava'. On careful perusal we also find that the decisions as well as the unreported decision as referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioner have no manner of application under the facts and circumstances of the present case.

30. However, in course of hearing of the rule the learned Advocate for the petitioner filed an application for referring the writ petition to the Hon'ble Chief Justice for decision by a full Bench under Rule 6 of Chapter 7 of the Supreme Court; (High Court) Rules, 1973 on the ground that the petitioner has come to know from reliable source that this Division Bench has discharged the rule in a similar case being Writ Petition No. 14606 of 2012 upon differing with the views of many other Division Benches. As such the Writ Petition is required to be referred to the Hon'ble Chief Justice for decision by a full Bench.

31. On heating the Learned Advocate and on perusal of the application we do not find any specific reason to justify the applicability of rule 6 of Chapter 7 of the High Court Division Rules; 1973, when there is specific guideline from 'the Appellate Division as mentioned above. As such we do not find any Substance in the application for referring this rule before the Hon'ble Chief Justice for decision by a full Bench under Rule 6 of Chapter 7 of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh (High Court Division) Rules, 1973. Accordingly prayer of the petitioner is rejected.

32. In view of the above. We hold that the impugned order does not suffer from any illegality warranting our interference. As such the respondents have no bar to do the needful in pursuance of the impugned Memo dated 11-4-2013 (Annexure-C) to appoint a Nikah Registrar in accordance with law.

33.	In the result, the Rule is discharged.

34.	The order of stay granted the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated.

However, there will be no order as to costs.

End.
